item.title: The Eames molded-plywood chair: shaping a material
item.description:
The Eames molded-plywood chairs show how a manufacturing process can shape both a product’s form and its assembly. Charles and Ray Eames explored bent plywood in the early 1940s. During World War II, the United States Navy commissioned them to develop molded-plywood splints, stretchers, and glider shells. Herman Miller’s design history describes how that work advanced their molding process.

Let the material set the boundary

After the war, the Eameses applied the process to chairs. Their first idea used one continuous shell, but the plywood did not withstand stress where the seat met the back. They changed to separate molded panels. The chair’s shape and joint followed the material’s limits.

item.title: Roxo Flex
item.description:
Roxo Flex is a Hugo theme for studios, teams, and project portfolios. Each site controls its own brand, content, section order, and visual style.

The design problem

The original theme supplied a useful page structure, but its templates used deprecated Hugo data access. Its counter fields also disagreed with the supplied example data. Roxo Flex keeps the portfolio layout and rebuilds the theme for current Hugo.

The system

Site owners set colors, type, spacing, icons, and image treatment in their Hugo configuration. The homepage reads its sections and order from a content file. The theme supplies layouts and reusable content patterns; each site supplies its own images and words.

item.title: Fairphone Gen. 6: making repair part of the product
item.description:
Repairability depends on more than a replaceable battery. A product also needs a clear access path, suitable fasteners, available parts, and instructions. Fairphone’s Gen. 6 provides a recent example of these choices working together.

Plan for service access

Fairphone’s July 2025 product announcement says the Gen. 6 has twelve replaceable parts and can be opened with one screwdriver. The listed parts include the battery, screen, camera, and USB port. Its repair guide shows the replacement steps for these assemblies.

item.title: Siteman
item.description:
Siteman is a static site manager for Hugo. It is delivered as a devenv module and provides commands to initialize, preview, build, and check a site.

The system

Siteman keeps authored content at the repository root. It keeps Hugo configuration, layouts, and archetypes under .siteman/. The file structure stays visible to site authors while the build tools remain contained.

The module supplies Hugo Extended and the siteman-* commands. A site can pin its theme as a Hugo module, build into public/, and validate local links before deployment.
